HAYKALAH contacts people only through haykalah.com and @haykalah.com email addresses.

Last updated 17 October 2026. We review this notice regularly and may update it.

On this page

  1. 01Our official channels
  2. 02What HAYKALAH never does
  3. 03Warning signs
  4. 04How to check a message
  5. 05How to report
  6. 06Questions

People sometimes use the names of established firms to make fake investment offers. This page lists HAYKALAH’s official channels, what HAYKALAH never does, and how to check and report a message that uses our name.

HAYKALAH does not offer investments, and nothing on this website is an offer, a solicitation or investment advice.

01Our official channels

Website
haykalah.com
Email
addresses that end in @haykalah.com, such as haykalah@haykalah.com
LinkedIn
linkedin.com/company/Haykalah, our company page, where we publish news and insights

HAYKALAH publishes no phone or WhatsApp number. A message that claims to be from HAYKALAH and reaches you any other way is not from an official channel.

02What HAYKALAH never does

  • It never asks for payments to personal accounts.
  • It never offers investments by WhatsApp, social media or messaging apps.
  • It does not sell securities, fund units or tokens, and it does not offer investments to the public.
  • It never asks for money or personal documents through any channel other than those listed above.

Regulated activities are executed through appropriately licensed partners. HAYKALAH is not an Authorised Person of the Capital Market Authority.

Regulatory status

03Warning signs

  • An investment offer, or a promise of returns, made in HAYKALAH’s name.
  • Pressure to decide or pay quickly, or to keep the offer secret.
  • A request to pay into a personal account, or into an account that does not belong to the company you are dealing with.
  • An email address that only looks like ours: an extra word or letter, or a different ending after “haykalah”.
  • A request for copies of your ID, bank details or passwords.

04How to check a message

  1. 1Do not reply to the message, and do not open its links or attachments.
  2. 2Write to us separately. Type haykalah@haykalah.com yourself in a new email, rather than replying, and tell us what you received.
  3. 3Wait for our answer before you pay, sign or send any document.

05How to report

  • Tell us at haykalah@haykalah.com. Include the sender’s details and a copy or screenshot of the message.
  • Report it to the relevant Saudi authorities, especially if money or personal documents were requested.
  • If you have already paid, contact your bank straight away.

06Questions

Does HAYKALAH offer investments?

No. HAYKALAH does not offer investments, and nothing on this website is an offer, a solicitation or investment advice. Where a transaction involves an offer of securities, that activity is carried out by a CMA-authorised institution engaged for the transaction.

Does HAYKALAH use WhatsApp?

HAYKALAH publishes no WhatsApp number, and it never offers investments by WhatsApp or social media.

Someone offered me tokens or Sukuk “with HAYKALAH”. Is it genuine?

HAYKALAH does not sell securities, fund units or tokens. Check with us at haykalah@haykalah.com before you do anything else.

How do I know an email really comes from HAYKALAH?

Our email addresses end in @haykalah.com. If in doubt, write to haykalah@haykalah.com from a new email, rather than replying, and ask us.
